summary: Body temperature is tracked per body part; prolonged exposure to cold or heat imposes stat penalties, pain, and can cause frostbite or heatstroke.

level_progression.recommendation: Maintain layered clothing appropriate to the season
Add insulating layers or seek shelter from wind
Light a fire, drink hot liquids, and insulate extremities
Emergency: build fire, change into dry clothing, apply heat packs
Immediately warm affected limbs with heat sources or retreat indoors
Hydrate, remove insulating layers, avoid strenuous activity
Cool down with shade or cold water immediately; rest until temperature stabilizes

environmental_factors.impact: Rapidly lowers exposed body part temperature when outdoors
Doubles heat loss until garments dry
Stabilize temperature while active and fueled
Fires, braziers, stoves, and hotplates raise nearby temperature
Winter storms and heat waves shift baseline temperature drastically

warning_signs: Status panel shows blue (cold) or red (hot) arrows per body part.
Log messages such as "Your hands are getting very cold" or "You feel feverishly hot" appear.
Focus drops sharply and pain climbs when frostbite risk is imminent.

cold: Layer clothing with high warmth and low encumbrance (e.g., wool socks, survivor armor).
Keep spare dry garments and blanket in base or vehicle.
Carry fire-starting kits (fire drill, lighter, tinder) to establish emergency heat.
Consume hot meals or drinks to gain temporary warmth bonus.
heat: Wear light, breathable clothing; remove helmets or coats when safe.
Travel during dawn/dusk, resting in shade during peak heat.
Drink clean water frequently; craft makeshift funnels for steady supply.
Use wet towels or jump into water to cool down when overheating warnings trigger.

monitoring_actions.action: Open character status screen to inspect per-limb temperature
Adjust clothing layers to respond to cold or heat
Craft heat-management gear such as survivor hoodies or improvised scarves
Activate portable heaters or thermal gear
